{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-fable-5-1","id":"msg_011CgM5zRvurMqwEvZXKdng2","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The Floyd-Warshall benchmark now runs unconditionally on the GPU with CUDA. Only the two existing files were changed, the executable is still `floydwarshall`, and no new files remain in the project.\n\n**What changed**\n\n- `floydwarshall/floydwarshall.cpp` now implements a blocked (tiled) Floyd-Warshall on the GPU. Each round runs three kernels: the diagonal tile, the tiles in that tile row and column, and all remaining tiles. Tiles are 64×64 with 16×16 threads, each computing a 4×4 register block from shared memory.\n- The matrix is padded to a multiple of 64 with unreachable dummy nodes, so any node count works.\n- `floydwarshall/CMakeLists.txt` enables the CUDA language, compiles the existing .cpp as CUDA via a source-file property, defaults to architecture 86 when none is given, and splits the compile flags by language.\n\n**Preserving exact semantics, including the path matrix**\n\nThe blocked algorithm gives the same distances as the sequential one, but naively it records different predecessor nodes. The sequential code's path entry equals the smallest intermediate-node bound at which the final distance is first reached. To reproduce that exactly, each cell carries a 64-bit key packing the distance in the high word and \"largest intermediate node plus one\" in the low word. Relaxation keeps the lexicographically smaller pair, which is a single unsigned 64-bit compare. That makes the blocked result bit-identical to the original for both matrices. The timed region includes device allocation and all transfers.\n\n**Verification**\n\nDistance hashes from the `-r` output match the original CPU build at every tested size. Path-matrix hashes were also compared using a temporary instrumented copy outside the project and match as well. Validation with `-v` passes.\n\n| Nodes | CPU original | GPU | Dist and path hashes match |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1, 2, 7, 100 | 0-1 ms | 0 ms | yes |\n| 512 | 165 ms | 2 ms | yes |\n| 1000 | 1143 ms | 7 ms | yes |\n| 2048 | 9411 ms | 23 ms | yes |\n| 4096 | not run | 95 ms | n/a |\n| 8192 | not run | 554 ms | n/a |\n\nA 32×32-thread variant was slightly slower, so the 16×16 layout was kept. I could not run compute-sanitizer because its injection library is missing on this machine. The build directory I used for testing was deleted from the project."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":32,"cache_creation_input_tokens":964,"cache_read_input_tokens":52793,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":964},"output_tokens":743,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global","speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"3d8adaf0-3b90-4971-806b-72df727157de","uuid":"f92f93a2-22c0-458d-a735-453516f3cbbc","timestamp":"2026-10-24T12:47:24.533Z","request_id":"req_011CgM5zRbKtQgTT3FQv5eZ6"}
